---
title: "The nine-species benchmark, version by version"
subtitle: "Every public copy of the benchmark, compared spectrum by spectrum"
description: "The nine-species de novo sequencing benchmark exists in at least eleven public versions. Every spectrum followed from one to the next: splits, labels, precursors, peaks, and how much of one version's test set another version trained on."
---

"Evaluated on nine-species" names at least eleven different sets of spectra.
This page puts every public copy of the benchmark on one key, *(species, raw
file, scan)*, and follows each spectrum from one version to the next: whether
it stays, which split it lands in, whether its label changes, and whether the
spectrum itself does. It was computed on 2026-10-20 from the files as
published that day; every number is an exact count unless it says otherwise.
The code is in
[`analysis/nine_species/`](https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/tree/main/analysis/nine_species),
and the catalog's own record of the versions is the
[nine-species benchmark's page](../datasets/nine-species-benchmark.html).

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Four things to know before quoting a nine-species number.**

1. **MSV000090982 is not the published benchmark.** It holds three builds, from
   2022, 2023 and 2024. The published one is a fourth, on Zenodo, and even the
   2024 build is 47,640 spectra away from it.
2. **The InstaNovo split, which NovoBench trains on, overlaps the test sets of
   the newer versions.** 17% of ProteoBench's spectra, 22% of dIon's test set and
   22% of denovo_benchmarks' nine-species sets are scans from its training split.
3. **One revised spectrum in six has a precursor on an isotope peak.** A model
   that enforces the precursor mass with no isotope allowance cannot get those
   right; on the original and on the InstaNovo split that never happens.
4. **The original writes every leucine as I.** Fold I and L before comparing
   labels across versions.
:::

## The versions

| version | where | spectra | made by |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **original** | MSV000081382, `HighResolution/data/high.<species>/peaks.db.mgf` | 1,528,127 | PEAKS DB exports, one MGF per species ([DeepNovo, 2017](../publications/de-novo-peptide-sequencing-by-deep-learning.html)) |
| original folds | same deposit, `cross.9high_80k.exclude_<species>` | 9 × 555,000 to 598,000 | about 80,000 spectra per species sampled once (mouse and *V. mungo* whole); each fold drops one species and splits the rest into train, valid and test |
| **InstaNovo split** | Hugging Face `InstaDeepAI/ms_ninespecies_benchmark` | 639,286 | the yeast-excluded fold's train (499,402) and valid (28,572), plus the original yeast file as test (111,312) |
| **MassIVE 2022** | MSV000090982, `peak/` | 2,812,194 | the first revised search: Tide and Percolator over ThermoRawFileParser MGFs, no N-terminal modifications |
| **MassIVE 2023** | MSV000090982, `updates/2023-03-08_woutb_2c43c18c` | 2,854,651 | a re-search; identical, record for record, to InstaNovo's `data/ninespecies_updated` |
| **MassIVE 2024** | MSV000090982, `updates/2024-05-14_woutb_71950b89` | 2,844,905 | the 2023 search, with peptides shared between species redrawn |
| **Zenodo main** | `10.5281/zenodo.13685813` | 2,838,117 | the published benchmark ([Wen & Noble, 2024](../publications/a-multi-species-benchmark-for-training-and-validating-mass-spectrometry.html)), the first build with no backbone in two species |
| **Zenodo balanced** | same record | 779,879 | 150 whole raw files of main, chosen to even out the species |
| **ProteoBench** | `nine_species_balanced_De_Novo.mgf.gz` | 779,879 | balanced, record for record, with the species dropped and the scans renumbered |
| **dIon** | Hugging Face `alfred-n/dIon-datasets` | 188,512 | a subset of main: 3,653 peptides per species for test, 100 for validation |
| **denovo_benchmarks** | MSV000096182, `9_species_*` | 946,155 | 101 raw files relabelled by the living benchmark's own search |

A **backbone** is the bare sequence with I and L folded together, the grain at
which two labels can be the same peptide.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  O["original 2017<br/>1,528,127"] --> F["9 folds<br/>~555k each"]
  F --> I["InstaNovo split<br/>639,286"]
  O -->|"yeast file = test"| I
  R["raw files"] --> C["converted MGFs<br/>15,165,161"]
  C --> M22["MassIVE 2022<br/>2,812,194"]
  C --> M23["MassIVE 2023<br/>2,854,651"]
  M23 --> M24["MassIVE 2024<br/>2,844,905"]
  C --> Z["Zenodo main<br/>2,838,117"]
  Z --> B["balanced<br/>779,879"]
  B --> P["ProteoBench<br/>779,879"]
  Z --> D["dIon<br/>188,512"]
  C --> DB["denovo_benchmarks<br/>946,155"]
```

The original and the revised benchmark share raw files and nothing else: the
revised benchmark re-converted every raw file, re-searched it, and relabelled
it. The three MassIVE builds, Zenodo main and denovo_benchmarks share the
converted peak lists: a spectrum present in two of them has the same precursor,
charge, retention time and peaks (denovo_benchmarks drops a few peaks per
spectrum). What differs between them is which spectra are in and what each is
labelled.

## Where the original's spectra went

Half of the original's 1,528,127 labelled spectra are in Zenodo main. Each of
the others was dropped at a step of the revised pipeline that can be named, by
asking the revised search itself about that scan.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
fate_order = ["kept in main", "raw file not in the revised search", "no target PSM for the scan",
              "failed 1% FDR, same peptide", "failed 1% FDR, other peptide",
              "passed, but the MGF gives no precursor charge",
              "passed, but its peptide was drawn for another species"]
// The CSV's columns are numbered steps of the pipeline ("3a failed ..."); the number names the fate.
// Parenthesised: in OJS `name = {...}` is a block, not an object literal.
fate_of = ({"0": 0, "1": 1, "2": 2, "3a": 3, "3b": 4, "4a": 5, "4c": 6})
fate_rows = ns.fate_by_species.flatMap(r => Object.entries(r)
  .filter(([k]) => k !== "species")
  .map(([k, v]) => ({species: r.species, fate: fate_order[fate_of[k.split(" ")[0]]], n: v})))
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 1000), height: 330, marginLeft: 110, marginBottom: 40,
  x: {label: "Share of the original's spectra in that species", percent: true, labelOffset: 34},
  y: {label: null, domain: d3.groupSort(fate_rows, g => -d3.sum(g.filter(d => d.fate === fate_order[0]), d => d.n) / d3.sum(g, d => d.n), d => d.species)},
  color: {domain: fate_order, range: ["#16a34a", "#94a3b8", "#cbd5e1", "#fbbf24", "#d97706", "#7c3aed", "#2563eb"],
          legend: true, columns: 2},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(fate_rows, Plot.stackX({offset: "normalize", order: fate_order,
      x: "n", y: "species", fill: "fate", tip: {format: {x: false}, channels: {Spectra: "n"}}})),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

| fate | spectra | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| kept in main | 762,973 | 49.9% |
| raw file not in the revised search (honeybee `BM-2`) | 22,757 | 1.5% |
| the revised search reported no target PSM for the scan | 305,624 | 20.0% |
| best PSM failed the 1% FDR, same peptide as the original | 130,599 | 8.5% |
| best PSM failed the 1% FDR, another peptide | 239,294 | 15.7% |
| passed, but the converted MGF gives no precursor charge | 37,179 | 2.4% |
| passed, but its peptide was found in several species and drawn for another | 29,701 | 1.9% |

Every scan the revised search reported nothing for was converted and searched;
its best match was simply a decoy, or nothing at all. Of the 762,973 kept,
705,828 keep their backbone and their modifications, 44,275 keep the backbone
with different modifications, and 12,870 are relabelled as another peptide.

## From raw files to main, and a filter the paper does not mention

Zenodo also publishes the converted MGFs before any search, which lets the
whole pipeline be replayed in counts.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
funnel = {
  const all = ns.converted.find(d => d.species === "ALL")
  return [
    {step: "MS2 spectra converted", n: all["converted MS2"]},
    {step: "best Percolator match is a target", n: all["target PSM"]},
    {step: "that PSM has q < 0.01", n: all["q<0.01"]},
    {step: "and the MGF gives a charge", n: all["q<0.01"] - all["q<0.01, no charge"]},
    {step: "Zenodo main", n: 2838117}
  ]
}
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 1000), height: 230, marginLeft: 230, marginRight: 80, marginBottom: 40,
  x: {label: "Spectra (millions)", transform: d => d / 1e6, labelOffset: 34},
  y: {label: null, domain: funnel.map(d => d.step)},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(funnel, {x: "n", y: "step", fill: "#2563eb"}),
    Plot.text(funnel, {x: "n", y: "step", text: d => d3.format(",")(d.n), dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11}),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

**Not one spectrum in main lacks a precursor charge**, although 2,345,279 of
the converted spectra do and the search ran on all of them: 62% of the human
spectra, 56% of *C. endoloripes*' and 15% of *B. subtilis*'. Percolator accepted
75,693 of them and every one was dropped. Wen & Noble do not describe this step.
They report dropping "13 MGF files with fewer than 100 accepted PSMs", and those
are 13 *B. subtilis* files in which no spectrum has a charge at all (103 to 397
accepted PSMs each, and a DIA run with 1): they fall under 100 only once the
charge-less ones are gone. Four mouse files with almost nothing accepted leave
339 raw files in main. Subtracting the charge-less spectra and those four files
gives 2,898,614, the paper's 2,898,611 within 3, and the shared-peptide draw
then removes 60,497 more. denovo_benchmarks applies the same charge filter when
it builds a dataset.

## What changed in the spectra that stayed

The original was exported by PEAKS in 2017 and the revised benchmark by
ThermoRawFileParser in 2022, and the two disagree about the spectrum itself.

**The precursor m/z.** Among the 801,288 spectra the original shares with the
2022 build, 15% have a neutral precursor mass 1 or 2 Da heavier in the revised
version. Every precursor in the original sits on its label's monoisotopic peak;
ThermoRawFileParser writes the m/z the instrument selected, which is often an
isotope peak. The revised search "allowed for 1 isotope error in the selection
of candidate peptides" (Wen & Noble, Methods), and the released MGFs keep the
instrument's m/z.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Column in the data -> label on the page.
iso_versions = new Map([["MassIVE r2022", "MassIVE 2022"], ["MassIVE r2023", "MassIVE 2023"],
                        ["MassIVE r2024", "MassIVE 2024"], ["Zenodo main", "Zenodo main"],
                        ["Zenodo balanced = ProteoBench", "balanced = ProteoBench"], ["dIon", "dIon"]])
iso_rows = ns.isotope_by_species.flatMap(r => [...iso_versions].map(([col, label]) => ({species: r.species, version: label, pct: r[col]})))
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 1000), height: 420, marginLeft: 110, marginBottom: 40,
  x: {label: "Spectra whose precursor is the label's M+1 peak (%)", domain: [0, 32], labelOffset: 34},
  y: {label: null, domain: d3.groupSort(iso_rows, g => -d3.mean(g, d => d.pct), d => d.species)},
  color: {domain: [...iso_versions.values()], scheme: "tableau10", legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleY(d3.groups(iso_rows, d => d.species).map(([s]) => s), {stroke: "#e2e8f0"}),
    // One mark per version, each nudged vertically: the builds sit within a
    // point of each other and drew on top of one another. dy is a constant in
    // Plot, not a channel, which is why this is six marks and not one.
    ...[...iso_versions.values()].map((v, i) =>
      Plot.dot(iso_rows.filter(d => d.version === v), {x: "pct", y: "species", fill: "version", r: 4,
               dy: (i - 2.5) * 6, stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.5, tip: true})),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

Over Zenodo main it is 484,359 spectra, 17.1%, from 1.6% of *V. mungo* to 24.8%
of yeast; 13.6% of ProteoBench's. The original, the InstaNovo split and
denovo_benchmarks have none. These are isotope picks and not missed
deamidations, which sit 0.019 Da away: the mass difference centres on 1.003 Da,
the error assuming a carbon-13 offset has a median of 1.0 ppm against 11.0 ppm
assuming deamidation, and 74,170 of the offset spectra have no N or Q to
deamidate. Casanovo's default allows an offset of 0 or 1; check what a given
model does before comparing its numbers across the two.

**The peaks.** The original's peak lists are sparser (median 142 peaks against
334) and reach fragment m/z values no fragment of the precursor can have (up to
47,568, against 5,496). For mouse, where both sides could be downloaded whole,
19,993 spectra were compared peak by peak: a median 97.6% of the original's
peaks are in the revised peak list within 10 ppm, carrying 97.0% of its
intensity, and the original's intensities are about 2.5 times the revised
ones. The original is the same scan after PEAKS's own processing.

**Everything else** barely moves: 20 of 801,288 shared spectra change charge,
every retention time agrees within 1 s, and the revised builds hold no charge-1
spectra (the original has 0.24%) and no peptide shorter than 6 or longer than 50
residues (the original runs from 5 to 65).

**The modification vocabulary.** The original and the 2022 build carry
oxidation, N and Q deamidation and carbamidomethylation. From 2023 on, four
N-terminal modifications appear: acetylation (+42.01), carbamylation (+43.01),
ammonia loss (-17.03) and carbamylation with ammonia loss (+25.98), on 6.6% of
main's spectra. A model trained on the original or on the InstaNovo split has
never seen one.

## Between the revised builds

| | out | in | label changed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MassIVE 2022 → 2023 | 199,297 | 241,754 | 41,389 |
| MassIVE 2023 → 2024 | 28,674 | 18,928 | 0 |
| MassIVE 2024 → Zenodo main | 27,214 | 20,426 | 0 |

**2022 to 2023 is a re-search.** 83% of the spectra leaving, and 83% of those
arriving, have a peptide the other build keeps in the same species: different
scans of the same peptide passed the FDR. Of the 41,389 relabelled spectra,
21,818 gain, lose or move an N or Q deamidation, 1,226 gain an N-terminal
modification, 10,775 move an I/L or a modification, and 7,570 change peptide.

**After 2023 every change is the shared-peptide draw.** Wen & Noble give each
peptide found in more than one species to one species at random and drop its
spectra from the others. Re-running that draw moves whole peptides between
species files: 28,673 of the 28,674 spectra leaving between 2023 and 2024, and
all 20,426 arriving between 2024 and Zenodo, carry a peptide found in more than
one species. Backbones present in more than one species file: 855 in 2022,
1,458 in 2023, 353 in 2024, and 0 in Zenodo main. The benchmark repository
cannot regenerate any of them exactly: its seed is fixed, but the species and
file order it draws over come from the filesystem.

## denovo_benchmarks' nine species

The living benchmark's datasets file calls its nine-species sets "De novo
nine-species benchmark (MSV000090982)". They are not. Its own deposit,
[MSV000096182](../datasets/de-novo-peptide-sequencing-tools-benchmark.html),
holds 101 raw files relabelled by its own search: 946,155 labels, keyed as
`<raw file>_<chunk>:<index>` into MGF chunks of at most 20,000 charged spectra.

- **A different subset of files.** Mouse takes all 13 raw files, including the
  four main drops; *B. subtilis* takes 4 of 106 and yeast 3 of 27; and honeybee
  includes `BM-2`, the file the revised search never had.
- **Different labels.** Of the spectra it shares with Zenodo main (478,000),
  87.6% carry the same label. 467,000 of its spectra, half, are not in main
  at all. 188,000 labels carry a modification the revised search did not
  allow: N-terminal, D, E and H carbamidomethylation, sodium on D and E, lysine
  and arginine methylation, and +12 and +26 N-terminal adducts.
- **A deamidation where the others see an isotope peak.** On 44,464 spectra
  that main labels at the M+1 peak, denovo_benchmarks writes the same backbone
  with one more deamidation in 39,011 cases. The carbon-13 reading fits better
  for 37,982 of them (median error 0.9 ppm against 12.1 ppm), so about 4% of
  these labels most likely carry a deamidation that is not there.
- **A deposit that does not match its labels in two files.** 1,014 labels point
  past the end of their MGF chunk (`BC-2_1` holds 18,996 spectra and is cited up
  to index 19,933), so those chunks are not the files the labels were made from.

## Splits, and what a model has already seen

**The original folds are disjoint on the modified peptide, not on the
backbone.** No validation or test label of a fold is a training label of that
fold, but 29 to 36% of every fold's validation and test spectra carry a backbone
it trains on, in another modification state. Across species, the held-out
species' spectra whose backbone the fold trained on run from 0.4% (*M. mazei*)
to 22.6% (*V. mungo*). The revised benchmark was built to remove that, and did:
no backbone in Zenodo main is in two species.

**The InstaNovo split is the original's yeast fold**, the same 499,402 training
spectra NovoBench retrains on: its train and valid are that fold's, and its test
set is the whole original yeast file. **Training on it and testing on another
version outside yeast tests partly on training data**, because the spectra are
the same physical scans, re-labelled.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
leak_rows = ns.leak.filter(d => !d["evaluate on"].startsWith("InstaNovo valid")).flatMap(d => [
  {set: d["evaluate on"], what: "its backbone is in the training split", pct: d["peptide seen %"]},
  {set: d["evaluate on"], what: "the same scan is in the training split", pct: d["same spectrum %"]}])
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 1000), height: 300, marginLeft: 260, marginRight: 30, marginBottom: 40,
  x: {label: "Share of the evaluation spectra (%)", domain: [0, 80], labelOffset: 34},
  y: {label: null, domain: [...new Set(leak_rows.map(d => d.set))]},
  color: {domain: ["its backbone is in the training split", "the same scan is in the training split"],
          range: ["#cbd5e1", "#dc2626"], legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(leak_rows.filter(d => d.what.startsWith("its")), {x: "pct", y: "set", fill: "what"}),
    Plot.barX(leak_rows.filter(d => d.what.startsWith("the same")), {x: "pct", y: "set", fill: "what", insetTop: 5, insetBottom: 5}),
    Plot.text(leak_rows.filter(d => d.what.startsWith("its")), {x: "pct", y: "set", text: d => `${d.pct.toFixed(1)}%`, dx: 5, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 10}),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

ProteoBench's yeast and *B. subtilis* spectra are untouched, but 71% of its mouse
spectra and half its human ones are scans a NovoBench-style model was trained
on. A number such a model scores on ProteoBench, on main beyond the yeast file,
on dIon or on denovo_benchmarks is partly a training score.

## What to write when reporting a number

- **Name the build, not the accession.** "Revised nine-species" is three builds
  under one MassIVE accession plus the Zenodo record; the InstaNovo IPC copy is
  the 2023 build; denovo_benchmarks is a selection of its own.
- **Do not train on the InstaNovo or NovoBench split and test on a newer
  version outside yeast.** Up to 22% of the test spectra are training scans, and
  about 60% carry a backbone the model trained on.
- **Allow a one-dalton precursor offset**, or score the revised spectra whose
  precursor is an isotope peak separately.
- **Fold I and L before comparing labels across versions.**
